beats.title: Port the prototype
beats.text: Flex's contract and CLI as switchboard review add | settle | working | log | answers, cards in .review/, and the page served by Switchboard so Send goes straight to the agent. prod-app's board moves onto it first: no more hand-edited HTML, no more copy-paste.

beats.title: Native Review in a project window
beats.text: SwiftUI rail, list and review mode, with card bodies in a web view; the Review pane beside the agent's terminal; the menu-bar count and popover.

beats.title: The project's picture
beats.text: The overview (phase strip, since you last looked, health, owed) and the Record.

beats.title: Every project
beats.text: The Review window, agent state on tiles, notifications you can answer, tear-off.

beats.title: The Mac, polished
beats.text: Full screen and Focus, Spotlight and ⌘K, Quick Look, drag and drop, the widget, the small touches.

beats.title: Away from the Mac
beats.text: Switchboard Mobile on Review's data contract: review mode, the overview glance, notifications you can answer. It's built on Fuchi's store client, lifted into a shared package, with pairing keys, sealed rows and per-device push.

options.label: This order
options.act: Steps 1–5 as listed, prod-app as the first user
options.then: Build in this order, with prod-app as the first project on it.

why: Step 1 is mostly porting work, because Flex has done the design and the build. It ends the copy-paste and the hand edits on the project you use every day, before anything native exists. Each step after it can be used on its own.
